title: introduce-invocation-provenance-and-cohorted-alerting
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: Long-tail token cost/latency regressions are noisy and often lack a clear lineage to the client invocation that caused them. This PR introduces a lightweight invocation provenance propagation layer and cohort-aware alerting to reduce alert churn and surface root causes faster.

What this changes (high level):
- Adds a provenance header (X-Redwood-Prov) propagated through the gateway, runtime, and downstream observability ingestion. The header carries a compact provenance token (base62) that maps to a transient lineage record.
- Emits new metrics: invocation_provenance.node_count, invocation_provenance.depth, invocation_cohort.id, token_segment_cost_usd, token_phase_latency_ms. These are low-cardinality summaries by design.
- Introduces a cohort fingerprinting step at the edge to group similar invocation shapes (prompt length, model family, presence of tools) into ephemeral cohorts used for alert dampening.
- Implements a cohorted alert damping controller: alerts are suppressed/muted for cohorts that are already being investigated, aggregated into cohort-level incidents, and use a backoff schedule to avoid duplicate notifications.
- Adds two new dashboards: Invocation Lineage Graph and Cohorted Cost Heatmap, and a small lineage table in the existing per-route cost explorer.
- Backwards compatible: clients that do not supply X-Redwood-Prov still work; runtime will synthesize a provenance token for the invocation.

Implementation notes:
- Provenance tokens are generated in the gateway (pkg/gateway/provenance.go) and attached as a header. A compact in-memory ring buffer stores recent lineage metadata (source_ip, route, model, timestamp) keyed by token. Lineage entries are emitted as a sparse event to the telem pipeline (telemetry/provenance/producer.go).
- The ingest pipeline was extended with a lightweight joiner (telemetry/provenance/joiner.py) that hydrates traces and metrics with provenance tokens when present and indexes cohort IDs into the metrics stream. We designed it to be stateless when provenance is absent.
- Alerting controller (pkg/alert/cohort_dampener.go) subscribes to cohort aggregations and marks alerts as coalesced when cohort-level incident is open. The controller exposes an API for on-call tools to claim cohorts.
- Dashboards: grafana panels added under obs/dashboards/invocation_lineage.json and obs/dashboards/cohort_heatmap.json. Panels include lineage flow, cohort size over time, median token cost per cohort, and long-tail invocation list.

Testing & CI:
- Unit tests for provenance generation and joiner logic. Integration test added to perf-canary that replays synthetic invocations and asserts provenance continuity.
- Initially a flakey ingestion test failed in CI due to a race on the ring buffer; root cause fixed by switching to an atomic cursor and rerun CI. Final CI status: pass.

Checklist:
- [x] Generate provenance token at gateway
- [x] Emit sparse lineage events to ingest pipeline
- [x] Hydrate traces/metrics with cohort ID
- [x] Add dashboards and wire links from per-route explorer
- [x] Add cohorted alert controller with claim API
- [x] Add unit + integration tests

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag (observability.provenance.enabled). Rolling rollout to 10% of gateway pods for canary, evaluate noise and alert reduction over 48h, then 100% if metrics stable.

Risks & mitigations:
- Cardinailty explosion: cohort fingerprints are designed low-cardinality (<= 512 active cohorts per deployment). We enforce eviction and TTL on lineage ring buffer.
- Privacy: provenance token contains no PII; lineage records redact client IPs before emission.
- Performance: provenance header adds ~50B to requests; joiner is async to avoid adding latency to request path.

Related: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-487/reduce-alert-churn-by-cohorting, support ticket SUP-3012 (customer investigations), and perf hub ENG-492 for canary scenarios.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice end-to-end. A couple of concerns: 1) ring buffer race — can you ensure atomic cursor updates? 2) cohort fingerprinting parameters should be configurable via flags. Please add tests for eviction behavior.

Aisha Patel: Addressed: switched ring buffer to atomic cursor (pkg/gateway/provenance.go), exposed cohort.window_size and cohort.max_active as runtime flags, added eviction unit tests (tests/integration/test_provenance.py).
Maya Singh: Left two small nits in the joiner (telemetry/provenance/joiner.py) — prefer dict.get with default and reduce allocations in hot path. Also can we cap emitted lineage fields to the schema?
Aisha Patel: Incorporated nits, limited emitted fields to the schema and added a fast path that avoids allocations when provenance absent.
Carlos Ramirez: Verified dashboards, cohort heatmap looks good. Integration perf-canary replay shows ~0.2% CPU overhead at 10% rollout. Approved.
release_notes: Add invocation provenance propagation and cohort-based alert dampening. New metrics (invocation_provenance.*, invocation_cohort.id, token_segment_cost_usd) and dashboards (Invocation Lineage Graph, Cohorted Cost Heatmap). Feature gated; rollout plan included.
